title: UK village hit by earthquake as houses shaken and 'loud boom' heard
excerpt: The tremor was recorded near Silverdale, Lancashire, at 8.38am today, with a magnitude of 2.7 on the Richter scale, with residents describing a 'loud boom'

14:37, 21 Sep 2026Updated 14:48, 21 Sep 2026

Neighbours in Lancashire have described hearing "loud bangs" and what sounded like a "lorry crashing into the house" as an earthquake hit the area.

‌

The tremor was recorded near Silverdale at 8.38am today, with a magnitude of 2.7 on the Richter scale. The British Geological Survey (BGS) explained it received reports of a "loud boom with weak shaking for a couple of seconds", with another one describing the earthquake as something "like a really strong explosion, rattled the doors and windows".

‌

According to BGS, the earthquake was recorded at a depth of 3km and had its epicentre near Silverdale. Nearby areas were also shaken.

‌

A report submitted to BGS described the tremor as something that "sounded like a lorry crashing into the house", LancsLive reports. The earthquake also sparked reaction on Facebook, as this was the second earthquake in a year to take place in Lancashire.

Previously, a 3.2 magnitude tremor shook the area in December but dozens of other smaller ones have taken place since. A resident on Coach Road in Warton said: "We are on Coach Road in Warton - the entire house shook. Definitely felt like the biggest so far!"

Another said: "Thought a truck had smashed into my house, was intense." Someone else wrote: "I wondered what the heck was going on - been running round the house trying to see if a tree fell over!"

Another Facebook user on Main Street said: "Two massive bangs and the whole house shook". Others said they felt the tremor further afield, with one person commenting: "I felt it in Morecambe", while another said: "Felt it Milnthorpe."
